title: Identification of fluid endocannabinoid and sphingolipid biomarkers in schizophrenia. A machine learning approach toward clinical value
title_zh: 识别精神分裂症中流体内大麻素和鞘脂生物标志物。一种用于临床价值的机器学习方法
abstract: Abstract Schizophrenia (SCZ) diagnosis relies on subjective clinical evaluation, with symptoms often overlapping between psychiatric conditions, hindering early intervention, and creating an urgent need for objective, accessible biomarkers. Lipids, especially endocannabinoid system (ECS) and sphingolipid metabolism members, are promising candidates given their implication in SCZ pathogenesis and measurability in accessible biofluids, with minimally invasive procedures. Our study conducted the first comprehensive crossover of endocannabinoids (eCBs) and sphingolipids in matched cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum samples from antipsychotic-naïve SCZ patients (SCZ naïve , n = 49), antipsychotic-treated patients (SCZ treat , n = 56), and healthy volunteers (HVs, n = 51). The machine learning Integrated Disease Explanation and Risk Scoring (IDEARS) platform was applied to eCBs, N-acylethanolamines, ceramides, and sphingomyelins quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, identifying key discriminatory features across biofluids and conditions (CSF AUC: SCZ naïve = 0.87, SCZ treat = 0.94; serum AUC: SCZ naïve = 0.87, SCZ treat = 0.90). Anandamide emerged as the top CSF feature in SCZ naïve patients, showing significantly elevated levels (q = 0.010) compared to HVs. Notably, though not statistically significant under conventional statistics, IDEARS identified anandamide as a top ten serum feature. Additionally, elevated sphingadiene backbone (d18:2) sphingolipids were conserved between the CSF and serum of SCZ naïve (q < 0.05), highlighting their potential as peripheral surrogate markers. Treatment-specific ceramide patterns were also evident, with elevated C16-C18 and reduced long-chain (>C24) species potentially reflecting antipsychotic metabolic effects. Our results support the involvement of the ECS and sphingolipid imbalances in SCZ, highlighting the potential of machine learning for novel biomarker discovery, including stratification across biofluids, and therapeutic monitoring toward more objective psychiatric care.
abstract_zh: 摘要 精神分裂症（SCZ）的诊断依赖于主观临床评估，不同精神疾病的症状常相互重叠，阻碍早期干预，迫切需要客观、易获取的生物标志物。脂质，特别是内源性大麻素系统（ECS）和鞘脂代谢成分，因其在精神分裂症病理机制中的作用以及在可获取生物液体中的可测量性，具有极大的潜力。本研究首次对匹配的脑脊液（CSF）和血清样本进行了全面的交叉分析，样本来自49名未服用抗精神病药物的精神分裂症患者（SCZ naïve），56名已服用抗精神病药物的患者（SCZ treat），以及51名健康志愿者（HVs）。研究人员应用基于液相色谱-串联质谱的内源性大麻素（eCBs）、N-乙醇胺、陶氏脂和鞘磷脂的机器学习整合疾病解释与风险评分（IDEARS）平台，鉴定出跨生物液体和条件的关键鉴别特征（CSF AUC：SCZ naïve = 0.87, SCZ treat = 0.94；血清 AUC：SCZ naïve = 0.87, SCZ treat = 0.90）。在SCZ naïve患者的CSF中，安南酰胺被确定为首要特征，其水平显著高于健康志愿者（q = 0.010）。值得注意的是，尽管在常规统计下未达到显著性，IDEARS平台仍在血清中将安南酰胺识别为前十特征之一。此外，SCZ naïve患者的CSF和血清中均保留了升高的鞘二烯骨架（d18:2）鞘脂，这突显了其作为周边替代标志物的潜力。此外，还观察到了治疗特异性的陶氏脂模式，即C16-C18链长升高，长链（>C24）物种减少，这可能反映了抗精神病药物的代谢效应。我们的研究结果支持内源性大麻素系统和鞘脂失衡在精神分裂症中的参与，突显了机器学习在新生物标志物发现中的潜力，包括跨生物液体的分层，以及向更客观精神病学护理过渡的治疗监测。
